output.summary: A perennial herb native to western North America, it grows from a layered bulb and bears grass-like leaves and blue, star-shaped flowers. Its bulbs are eaten after roasting or boiling, but are easily confused with toxic death-camas bulbs.
output.edibilityNote: Bulbs are roasted, boiled or made into flour; they are difficult to distinguish from poisonous death-camas bulbs.
